prerequisites: A crafted .org file must already exist in a public project
Planting that file normally requires authenticated project write access
Public repositories demonstrate the vulnerable rendering path, but not every repository demonstrates weaponized command execution
browserApiAssessment.publicPoc: Three XDB repositories implement the same anonymous rich blob-viewer trigger
browserApiAssessment.rationale: Multiple public exploit sources trigger the vulnerable Org renderer with an anonymous simple GET. It is not an /api route, but a hostile page can still send the request without reading the response. The content-seeding prerequisite makes the result conditional.
evidenceNotes: A fourth XDB source calls an /api/v4 raw-file endpoint, but describes the crasher and payload placement as pending, so that API call is not counted as a confirmed trigger.

vulnerabilities.summary: The Ruby SAML library is for implementing the client side of a SAML authorization. Ruby-SAML in <= 12.2 and 1.13.0 <= 1.16.0 does not properly verify the signature of the SAML Response. An unauthenticated attacker with access to any signed saml document (by the IdP) can thus forge a SAML Response/Assertion with arbitrary contents. This would allow the attacker to log in as arbitrary user within the vulnerable system. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.17.0 and 1.12.3.

browserThreatModel.description: Attacker-controlled public web page reaching an internal GitLab through an Edge 131-class browser.
assumptions: No stolen GitLab token and no attacker knowledge of victim credentials.
No ambient cross-site GitLab session cookie is assumed.
Edge 131 default Private Network Access warnings are not enforced.
GitLab /api/* and /api/graphql wildcard CORS responses are readable without credentials.
Simple cross-origin GET/form requests may be sent even when their non-API responses are not readable.

statuses.confirmed-compatible: Public primary reproduction establishes a browser-sendable trigger under this threat model.
statuses.likely-compatible: Official evidence strongly indicates compatibility, but exact primary reproduction details are unavailable.
statuses.conditional-compatible: Browser-call compatible only when listed content, configuration, identifiers, or scale prerequisites exist.
statuses.unresolved: Public evidence is insufficient to decide.
statuses.outside-threat-model: An explicit prerequisite or transport is outside this anonymous hostile-page model.

browserThreatModel.methodology: Every record receives a structured review. Anonymous network candidates not excluded by privileges, interaction, or transport are marked as manually reviewed only when a CVE-specific override records route, prerequisite, response-readability, and public-primary-reproduction findings; remaining candidates stay unresolved and are counted as pending manual review. Explicit privilege, interaction, and non-network blockers are classified from CVSS plus the official description. VulnCheck XDB is queried separately for every CVE; repository presence is supporting evidence, while sourceReview records whether the linked implementation was actually inspected. Outside-threat-model does not mean non-exploitable generally.
